text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager trigged: SmartRouting decision loop detected for customer-prod-42.  Error: route_fallback_count > 10 in 5m.

Anna (oncall): saw the pager, jumping in. Can someone paste the initial error logs?

Lee (sre): logs here — lots of repeated 'fallback to us-west-2 variant' events followed by 'no-capacity' then immediate fallback back to eu-west-1, loop. Suspect policy mismatch after recent rollout.

Carol (ml): noticed variants: 'redwood-rtq-v2' vs 'redwood-rtq-v2-quant'. Traffic pinned to quant variant in eu-west-1 but routing policy says prefer lower-cost variant in us-west-2 — that might be incompatible capacity-wise.

Jess (support): customers reporting increased 5xxs and timeouts since ~12:43 UTC. Several tickets opened: #5671, #5674. High-priority.

Anna (oncall): ok immediate mitigations: 1) pause smart-routing policy for affected customer 2) force-route to eu-west-1 stable variant 3) open oncall handoff if I need to step away. Who can flip policy?

Max (infra): I can patch the policy flag in config service. Where is the flag?

Carol (ml): policy is `service.route_policies.smart_routing.enabled`. But note: the decision logs are missing route tags for these fallbacks — hard to correlate which policy chose what.

Lee (sre): can we confirm decision log entries? I'm only seeing `route_decision=FALLBACK` without the `route_tag` field for ~1200 events. Looks like a logging regress from the change on 2026-02-10.

Anna (oncall): Max, please pause the smart_routing for customer-prod-42 now and set `force_route=eu-west-1:redwood-rtq-v2`.

Max (infra): doing now. Patching config:
```bash
curl -X POST https://config.internal/api/set -d '{"customer":"customer-prod-42","route_policies.smart_routing.enabled":false,"force_route":"eu-west-1:redwood-rtq-v2"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'
```
Max (infra): confirmed: flag set, routing control plane acknowledged.

incident-bot: Action recorded: smart_routing disabled for customer-prod-42 by Max.

Raj (product): any idea on customer impact window? Need to coordinate comms.

Jess (support): from tickets, peak 5xxs between 12:42–12:51 UTC. Estimated affected requests ~18k, ~3% of peak qps. Two customers reported degraded latency.

Carol (ml): while we mitigated, root cause likely policy mapping mismatch: a recent policy change added preference rules by cost-tier but didn't account for variant compatibility matrix. The routing engine tried to move traffic to us-west-2:quant but binaries there don't support the same KV-cache format, causing capacity rejects -> immediate fallback -> loop.

Lee (sre): agreed. But we need better observability: decision logs lack `route_tag` and `selected_variant` fields. Also missing `fallback_reason` codes in some events. That made triage slower.

Anna (oncall): logging gaps noted. For now, are we confident the force_route is stable? Any flapping?

Max (infra): route stable, no new fallback events for this customer after the change. System metrics show error rate back to baseline by 12:55 UTC.

Carol (ml): quick check: the quantized variant in us-west-2 had different context-length kernel, causing rejects when requests with >1024 tokens hit it. We should validate variant compatibility matrix in model catalog.

Lee (sre): I'm going to open a short-lived guard: disable cross-region fallback for policy group until we have compatibility checks. That should prevent loops cluster-wide.

Anna (oncall): please do, Lee. Also tagging this for oncall handoff — I'm going to bed in ~30m so I'll hand to Lee.

Lee (sre): I'll take over after your handoff. Quick checklist for post-incident:
- Collect decision logs for 12:40–12:56 UTC
- Add missing fields (`route_tag`,`selected_variant`,`fallback_reason`) to decision log schema
- Re-run compatibility validation for `redwood-rtq-v2-quant` in us-west-2
- Add an alert for fallback_count spike but only after route_tag present (to reduce noise)

Raj (product): also need customer impact summary. Jess can you prepare a short blurb for PG and affected customers? Include timeframe and mitigation steps.

Jess (support): will draft. Summary: "From ~12:42–12:55 UTC we observed degraded responses for customer-prod-42 due to smart routing selecting an incompatible model variant across regions leading to fallback loops. We disabled smart routing and forced traffic to the stable eu-west-1 variant; service has recovered. Postmortem forthcoming."

Carol (ml): long-term: add unit test in model onboarding that checks KV-cache compatibility, token limits, and kernel support across regions/quantization levels. Also add a model-variant compatibility table to the model catalog UI.

Lee (sre): I'm seeing a concurrent observability deploy that removed `route_tag` from structured logs — tagging @deploy-bot. Who approved that?

Anna (oncall): that was a low-risk logging change in infra last week. Max, can you confirm the deploy change?

Max (infra): yes confirmed — logging schema change landed 2026-02-10 in infra/logging. It accidentally omitted `route_tag` in the streaming logger for routing decisions. Rolling back the logging change is low-risk; I'll coordinate with infra team to revert today.

incident-bot: Note: oncall handoff scheduled. Anna -> Lee at 13:00 UTC.

Anna (oncall): handing over to Lee. All mitigation steps in place. Adding follow-ups: add decision-tagged trace view in console, enforce compatibility gate in rollout pipeline, update alerting threshold semantics.

Lee (sre): taking oncall. I'll keep monitoring for 2h and start the postmortem doc. Assigning owners:
- Logging rollback & schema fix: Max
- Compatibility tests & model catalog update: Carol
- Routing policy safety (disable cross-region fallback): Lee + Max
- Customer comms: Jess + Raj

Anna (oncall): thanks team. One more ask: please make sure decision logs include `route_tag` in both structured events and the fallback audit trail — that would have saved ~8min of triage.

Max (infra): noted. Rolling back logging change and adding unit test to prevent regressing again. ETA for rollback + re-deploy: 3h.

Jess (support): customer comms draft ready, pinging PGs.

Carol (ml): I started a quick compatibility job to run against current quant binaries; results show mismatch on cache format. I'll attach the output to the postmortem.

Lee (sre): closing the incident channel for now — if any new flapping occurs reopen. Postmortem link will be posted here when ready. Thanks. :white_check_mark:
